member.name: T:winapp2ool.browserbuildersettings
member.summary:
Holds the settings for the Browser Builder module, which allows winapp2ool to build bespoke entries for individual web browsers through a simple scripting interface.
Browser Builder reads all of its input files from a single source directory:
chromium.ini : Generative rulesets for Chromium-based browsers (BrowserInfo + EntryScaffold sections). Either this or gecko.ini must be present.
gecko.ini : Generative rulesets for Gecko/Goanna-based browsers (BrowserInfo + EntryScaffold sections). Either this or chromium.ini must be present.
browser_additions.ini : Sections and keys to add after generation (optional)
browser_section_removals.ini - Sections to remove after generation (optional)
browser_name_removals.ini - Keys to remove by name after generation (optional)
browser_value_removals.ini - Keys to remove by value after generation (optional)
browser_section_replacements.ini - Sections to replace after generation (optional)
browser_key_replacements.ini - Keys to replace by value after generation (optional)

member.name: T:winapp2ool.uwpbuildersettings
member.summary:
Holds the settings for the UWPBuilder module, which generates winapp2.ini entries for Universal Windows Platform applications from a small templating DSL.
Summary of UWPBuilder files and their expected content:
UWPFile1
Source directory — the root folder containing the UWP scaffold template ( UWP.ini ) and an AppInfo\ subdirectory whose per-letter *.ini files are combined at runtime to produce the full app list. Only the Dir of this chooser is used; the Name is ignored.
UWPFile2
Output file — where the generated UWP entries are written. This file is consumed by the build pipeline to produce the final winapp2.ini.
UWPFile3
Shared WebView scaffold catalog (typically Assembler\Scaffolds\webview.ini ). Source for [WebViewScaffold: ...] sections consumed when an AppInfo entry declares WebViewPath= . If the file is missing or empty, generation continues with zero WebView FileKeys emitted and a warning logged.
UWPFile4
Shared QtWebEngine scaffold catalog (typically Assembler\Scaffolds\qtwebengine.ini ). Source for [QtWebEngineScaffold: ...] sections consumed when an AppInfo entry declares QtWebEnginePath= . If the file is missing or empty, generation continues with zero QtWebEngine FileKeys emitted and a warning logged.

member.summary: The source directory containing the UWP scaffold template ( UWP.ini ) and the AppInfo\ subfolder with per-letter app definitions. Only the Dir property is used; Name is ignored.

member.name: T:winapp2ool.UWPBuilder
member.summary:
UWPBuilder is a winapp2ool module which handles the generation of winapp2.ini entries for Universal Windows Platform applications installed under %LocalAppData%\Packages .
It also allows for hybrid win32+UWP entries for applications that have both a UWP package and a win32 installation, by supporting importing arbitrary FileKey, DetectFile, Detect, ExcludeKey, and RegKey values from the AppInfo definitions.
It reads from a single source directory containing:
UWP.ini
The scaffold template with one or more [EntryScaffold: ...] sections. Each scaffold's DetectFileBase= lines are expanded per package to produce the entry's detection paths, and its FileKeyBase= lines are applied to every application as a consistent baseline set of cleaning targets.
An AppInfo\ subdirectory of per-letter *.ini files.
Each section describes one UWP application with its Package= identifier, category, optional Detect= , DetectFile= , and RegKey= keys, and any app-specific FileKeyBase= , FileKey= , and ExcludeKey= lines. These files are combined in-memory at runtime; no intermediate combined file is required.
The %Package% DSL variable expands to %LocalAppData%\Packages\<PACKAGE_FOLDER> . Apps with multiple packages use numbered variants: Package1= / Package2= in the source and %Package1% / %Package2% in key values.

Selects the set of WebViewScaffold names that should be emitted for the given app. Resolution order:
If the AppInfo declared WebViewScaffolds= (regardless of value), use that explicit list — a present-but-empty value yields no scaffolds, distinct from the "key absent → use defaults" case.
If the explicit list contains the sentinel All (case-insensitive), it is replaced with every scaffold name in . Any other names listed alongside All are redundant and emit a warning.
Otherwise, use .
Any names in are then subtracted, and unknown names (not present in ) are dropped with a warning. Combining WebViewScaffolds= and ExcludeWebViewScaffolds= warns when the explicit list is anything other than All , since exclusions usually pair with the implicit defaults. All + exclusions is the natural idiom for "everything except these" and does not warn.

The MenuSection receiving warnings for display

Summary of EntryBuilder files and their expected content:
EntryBuilderFile1
Source directory — the folder containing per-letter *.ini source files. Each section in those files describes one output entry; the section header is the output entry name. EntryBuilderFile4

member.name: T:winapp2ool.EntryBuilder
member.summary:
EntryBuilder is a winapp2ool module which generates winapp2.ini entries from a shorthand DSL. It reads per-letter source files under Assembler\EntryBuilder\*.ini , expands winapp2ool-private shorthand keys, and emits a standard winapp2.ini-style output file consumed by the build pipeline.
Each section in a source file describes one application and corresponds to exactly one output winapp2.ini entry: the section header is the entry name (e.g. [Discord *] ) and is round-tripped verbatim into the output. Any valid winapp2 key passes through unchanged, so a raw entry can be pasted into a source file and incrementally enriched with shorthand. The deprecated SpecialDetect= is refused: the key is dropped with a warning rather than passed through or misparsed as a variable declaration.
Scaffold families are the first shorthand category. An entry opts into a family by declaring one or more root paths for it: WebViewRoot= (one per WebView2 / EBWebView data root) or QtWebEngineRoot= (one per QtWebEngine profile directory). The module then expands the selected scaffolds — WebViewScaffolds= / ExcludeWebViewScaffolds= for WebView2, QtWebEngineScaffolds= / ExcludeQtWebEngineScaffolds= for QtWebEngine — into FileKey lines, substituting the family's placeholder ( %WebViewRoot% or %QtWebEngineRoot% ) against each declared root. The two families are independent: an entry may declare either, both, or neither. Non-scaffold targets are written via FileKeyBase= / RegKeyBase= with the same substitution rule (either placeholder). An entry without any root declaration emits no scaffold output, which is the correct default for entries that just want pass-through plus future shorthand. The DSL is open to additional scaffold catalogs in future (each introduces its own opt-in trigger key).
Recognised shorthand keys (stripped from output): WebViewRoot= , WebViewScaffolds= , ExcludeWebViewScaffolds= , QtWebEngineRoot= , QtWebEngineScaffolds= , ExcludeQtWebEngineScaffolds= , FileKeyBase= , RegKeyBase= , ExcludeKeyBase= , Skip= .
Scaffolds are loaded from two shared catalogs via : Assembler\Scaffolds\webview.ini ( %WebViewRoot% templates) and Assembler\Scaffolds\qtwebengine.ini ( %QtWebEngineRoot% templates), each substituted per declared root at generation time.
Unlike UWPBuilder , this module never emits Default= . Generated entries are opt-in by design to keep the cleaning UI uncluttered as small Electron apps proliferate.

member.name: F:winapp2ool.EntryBuilder.DefaultScaffolds
member.summary: Default scaffold names emitted when an entry does not declare an explicit WebViewScaffolds= selection. Limited to low-risk categories; host-risk scaffolds (cookies, history, session, web storage) require explicit opt-in by the entry author.

member.name: F:winapp2ool.EntryBuilder.NestedRefWatchThreshold
member.summary: Nested-reference count at or above which an entry's variable block is reported as a tangled abstraction in the run statistics. The trigger is interdependency, not raw variable count: real run data shows variable count flags the DSL's best work (e.g. an entry declaring 9 flat variables that fan out to 430 keys — a triumph, not a concern), whereas the genuinely hard-to-read blocks are the ones whose variables reference each other, forcing the reader to topologically sort a dependency graph. Across the source the distribution is near-bimodal — a large cluster at one nested ref (cheap one-hop convenience vars) and a small tail at 3-5 (the actual tangles) — so the threshold sits in that gap. Set to 4 to surface only the severe cases (ABBYY-, Acrobat- class); lower to 3 to also catch shallow multi-variable chains.

member.name: M:winapp2ool.EntryBuilder.inferRootDetection(winapp2ool.EntryBuilder.EntrySpec@,winapp2ool.MenuSection)
member.summary:
Synthesises detection from a reserved Root variable. When an entry declares Root= , EntryBuilder guarantees a Detect=<Root> (registry-domain root) or DetectFile=<Root> (filesystem-domain root) is present, classifying by the leading path segment of the resolved value against the known registry hives via . The synthesised key is the literal <Root> token rather than the expanded value, so the normal phase-2 pass in fans it out over multi-valued roots and marks Root referenced for the unreferenced-variable typo backstop.
Injection is idempotent and additive: if the target list already holds a <Root> token (a hand-written Detect=<Root> ) nothing is added, and any other detection criteria are left untouched. The token is prepended so the root anchor is the first detection key of its kind.
Authors who want a base-path variable WITHOUT automatic detection must name it something other than Root .
member.param: The entry being parsed; its / are mutated in place when a Root variable is present
The MenuSection receiving warnings for display

member.summary:
Selects the set of WebView scaffold names that should be emitted for the given entry. Resolution order:
If the entry declared WebViewScaffolds= (regardless of value), use that explicit list. A present-but-empty value yields no scaffolds.
If the explicit list contains the sentinel All (case-insensitive), it is replaced with every scaffold name in ; any other names listed alongside All are redundant and emit a warning.
Otherwise, use .
Any names in ExcludedWebViewScaffolds are then subtracted, and unknown names (not present in ) are dropped with a warning. Combining WebViewScaffolds= and ExcludeWebViewScaffolds= warns when the explicit list is anything other than All .

member.name: T:winapp2ool.CCiniDebug
member.summary:
CCiniDebug is a winapp2ool module which performs housekeeping on the CCleaner Classic (v1-6) configuration file ccleaner.ini to clean up leftovers from winapp2.ini
As entries are removed or renamed in winapp2.ini over time, stale configuration keys are leftover in ccleaner.ini. CCiniDebug processes a ccleaner.ini for its entry configuration keys and checks them each against the names of entries in winapp2.ini. Any configuration keys found with the winapp2.ini indicator (*) in the name which do not have a corresponding entry by the same name in the most recent winapp2.ini can then be easily and automatically removed

member.name: T:winapp2ool.Combine
member.summary:
Combine is a winapp2ool module that takes all files with the ini extension within a target directory (including its subdirectories) and combines them into a single ini file. When duplicate section names are encountered, their unique keys are merged together into the output and a warning lists the collisions; with strict name checking enabled (, -strict on the CLI), collisions instead fail the run — the output is not saved and a nonzero exit code is set — since the build pipeline's staged inputs are expected to be disjoint.
Files that cannot be parsed or have no sections are ignored.

member.summary: File system and registry locations which are considered too vague to be used to establish matching key content across entries on their own

member.name: P:winapp2ool.DiffConfiguration.IgnoredKeyTypes
member.summary:
Key types that are silently excluded from all diff comparisons. These keys carry no semantic information independent of the entry name and would produce only noise in diff output.
Currently: ID (CCleaner 7 format, duplicates the section name)

member.name: P:winapp2ool.DiffConfiguration.ClassifierKeyTypes
member.summary:
Key types that classify an entry into a category. At most one of these should appear per entry, so when the old and new key both belong to this set they are treated as an update rather than a remove + add.
LangSecRef and Section are the base format classifiers; Tags is the CCleaner 7 equivalent.

member.name: P:winapp2ool.DiffConfiguration.DetectionKeyTypes
member.summary:
Key types that establish an entry's detection criteria — how winapp2ool decides the target application is present. These are counted together (not per individual type) when deciding whether a detection change is a modification rather than a remove + add, because an entry's detection is a single conceptual role even when spread across several keys of mixed type.
Excludes DetectOS (an OS-version gate, handled as a defunct singleton) and SpecialDetect (deprecated).

member.name: F:winapp2ool.DiffConfiguration.BrowserSectionSubstring
member.summary: Substring matched (case-insensitive) against Section key values to identify web browser entries generated by BrowserBuilder

member.name: P:winapp2ool.DiffConfiguration.BrowserSecRefs

member.name: P:winapp2ool.DiffConfiguration.MovementKeySeparator
member.summary:
Separator character used in movement key signatures stored in KeyMovementTracker.MovedKeys.
Null character (Chr(0)) cannot appear in ini file key values, making it unambiguous as a delimiter

member.name: M:winapp2ool.KeyModificationAnalyzer2.PairDetectionCriteria(System.Collections.Generic.List{winapp2ool.iniKey2}@,System.Collections.Generic.List{winapp2ool.iniKey2}@)
member.summary:
Pairs detection-criteria changes as modifications, preferring the least ambiguous reading. An entry's detection criteria (its Detect and DetectFile keys) is a single conceptual role: how winapp2ool decides the target application is present.
Two passes run over the still-unmatched detection keys. First, any detection key type with exactly one added and one removed key is paired same-type — e.g. one DetectFile replaced by another at a different path. Then, if exactly one added and one removed detection key remain (necessarily of different types), they are paired as a cross-type swap — e.g. a Detect becoming a DetectFile. Any detection key that cannot be paired one-for-one this way is left as a plain add/remove, so a lone removed Detect alongside a matched DetectFile swap stays reported as removed.
member.param: The still-unmatched removed keys; paired detection keys are removed in place
The still-unmatched added keys; paired detection keys are removed in place
member.returns: Pairs of (new iniKey2, old iniKey2) for each one-for-one detection swap found, or an empty list if none qualify

member.summary: If exactly one added key and exactly one removed key satisfy , records them as a (new, old) pair in and removes both from and . Does nothing otherwise, so an ambiguous many-to-one or one-sided change is left untouched.
member.param: The still-unmatched removed keys; the matched key is removed in place
The still-unmatched added keys; the matched key is removed in place
The accumulator the matched (new, old) pair is appended to
Selects which keys participate in this swap (e.g. a specific detection key type)

member.name: M:winapp2ool.KeyModificationAnalyzer2.PairRegKeysBySharedPath(System.Collections.Generic.List{winapp2ool.iniKey2}@,System.Collections.Generic.List{winapp2ool.iniKey2}@)
member.summary:
Pairs RegKeys that share an identical registry path (the portion before the first | ) but target different value-names, promoting each such pair to an updated key.
Because the winapp2.ini format permits at most one value-name per RegKey, the registry path uniquely groups the value-names cleaned beneath it: a path with exactly one removed and one added RegKey is an unambiguous change to that key's cleaning rule rather than an independent removal and addition. Paths with more than one removed or added RegKey are left untouched, since which removal pairs with which addition cannot be determined.
member.param: The still-unmatched removed keys; promoted RegKeys are removed in place
The still-unmatched added keys; promoted RegKeys are removed in place
member.returns: Pairs of (new iniKey2, old iniKey2) for every registry path carrying exactly one removed and one added RegKey

member.name: T:winapp2ool.Diff
member.summary:
Compares two winapp2.ini format iniFile s and summarizes the changes to the user
NOTE: to "exist" here means for an entry of the same exact name (case sensitive) to exist
Changes fall three major categories:
Added entries exist in the new file and not in the old file
Modified entries exist in both the new file and the old file and have been changed in some way
Removed entries exist in the old file but not in the new file
Additionally, Removed entries have three sub categories:
Renamed entries do not exist in the new file, but their content exists in some other entry in the file, mostly unchanged from the old version (may contain minor changes)
Merged entries do not exist in the new file, but their content exists in some other entry in the new file which is substantially different from the old version
Removed without replacement do not exist in the new file and their content was not found in some other entry in the new file
Likewise, Merged entries themselves are broken into two categories
Modified Entries that existed in the old file which have been modified to contain content from entries which have been removed
Added Entries which did not exist in the old file but who contain content from entries which have been removed

member.name: F:winapp2ool.logger._logLock
member.summary: Synchronizes writes to GlobalLog . Per-thread paths (capture buffers) bypass this lock since they touch only thread-local state.

member.name: P:winapp2ool.logger.GlobalLog
member.summary: The global Winapp2ool log, containing everything logged during the current session

member.name: P:winapp2ool.logger.SaveGlobalLogOnExit
member.summary: When True , the global log is written to disk as the application exits, even on a clean silent-mode run. Set by the global -writelog command line flag. A nonzero process exit code saves the log independently of this flag, so scripted and CI runs always retain the diagnostics from a failed build.

member.name: F:winapp2ool.logger._nestCount
member.summary: Per-thread indentation depth. Each thread sees its own counter so that parallel work cannot corrupt the indentation of unrelated threads.
member.remarks: ThreadStatic fields default to zero on every thread that has not yet written to them, exactly the desired initial state. Threads spawned inside a parallel section start at depth zero regardless of the calling thread's depth; use gLogCapture to record those threads' output for later flush under the parent's depth.

member.name: F:winapp2ool.logger._captureBuffer
member.summary: When non- Nothing , gLog writes go to this thread-local buffer instead of GlobalLog . Set by gLogCapture and restored on dispose.

member.name: P:winapp2ool.logger.nestCount
member.summary: The current indentation level of the global log on the calling thread.

The String to be added into the log

Indicates that the should be added into the log
Optional, Default: True
Indicates that an empty line should be added into the log following
Indicates that an empty line should be added into the log before

member.name: M:winapp2ool.logger.gLog(System.Func{System.String},System.Boolean,System.Boolean,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Lazy overload of gLog . The lambda is invoked only when is True , avoiding allocations from string interpolation when the log call would have been suppressed.
member.param: Factory invoked to produce the log line. Not called when is False

member.name: M:winapp2ool.logger.gLogScope(System.String,System.Int32)
member.summary: Opens a nested logging scope. The optional is logged at the current depth, then the depth is increased by until the returned IDisposable is disposed. Use with Using to make ascend/descend imbalance impossible by construction.
member.param: Optional header line written before ascending. Pass "" for an anonymous scope
Number of indentation levels to ascend. Optional, default: 1

example.code: Using gLogScope("Beginning lint") ' nested gLog calls are indented one level deeper here End Using

member.name: M:winapp2ool.logger.gLogCapture
member.summary: Redirects the calling thread's gLog writes into a thread-local buffer until the returned object is disposed. Captured lines preserve their relative indentation (depth resets to zero on entry and restores on exit), so they can be replayed later under any parent depth via EmitCaptured .
member.returns: A LogCapture whose Lines contains the buffered output. The capture is active until Dispose is called (typically via Using )
member.remarks: Designed for parallel sections: each parallel task captures its own log slice, and the orchestrating thread emits the slices in deterministic order after the parallel work finishes. This eliminates the need for per-module deferred-log workarounds (see EntryLintResult.DiagLines ).

member.name: M:winapp2ool.logger.EmitCaptured(System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{System.String})
member.summary: Appends previously-captured lines to GlobalLog , indented at the calling thread's current depth. Acquires the log lock once for the whole batch.
member.param: The captured lines, as returned by LogCapture.Lines . Nothing is a no-op

member.name: T:winapp2ool.logger.LogScope
member.summary: Disposable handle returned by gLogScope . On dispose, restores the nesting depth that was in effect at construction.
member.remarks: Created and disposed on the same thread. Passing the handle to another thread for disposal would corrupt that thread's depth — don't do it.

member.name: T:winapp2ool.logger.LogCapture
member.summary: Disposable handle returned by gLogCapture . While alive, redirects the calling thread's gLog writes into Lines . Restores the previous capture buffer and nesting depth on dispose.
member.remarks: Captures nest correctly: an inner capture saves and restores the outer capture's buffer, so its lines flow back to the outer buffer rather than to GlobalLog .

member.name: P:winapp2ool.logger.LogCapture.Lines
member.summary: The captured lines, with relative indentation preserved.

member.name: F:winapp2ool.MenuMaker.VtClearScreen
member.summary: VT escape that homes the cursor and erases the entire screen. One atomic write to a VT-capable terminal replaces the three Win32 calls ( SetConsoleCursorPosition , FillConsoleOutputCharacter , FillConsoleOutputAttribute ) that Console.Clear performs internally.

member.name: M:winapp2ool.MenuMaker.clrConsole(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Clears the console when the given is True , output is not redirected, and output is not suppressed.
member.param:
Indicates that the console should be cleared
Optional, Default: True
member.remarks:
On a VT-capable terminal (Windows 10 1607+ conhost, Windows Terminal, anything UNIX-ish) this emits the VT clear escape, which is a single write. If a buffered render is active, the escape is appended to the buffer so the clear and the new menu arrive at the terminal in one atomic write — no flicker.
On legacy consoles (XP / Vista / 7 / pre-1607 Win10) falls back to Console.Clear . When output is redirected (test runner, pipeline silent mode, piped to a file) the call is a no-op — clearing a non-console sink would corrupt downstream output.

member.name: T:winapp2ool.TerminalCapabilities

Probes whether the attached console supports virtual terminal (ANSI/VT) escape sequences. On Windows 10 1607 (Aug 2016) and newer, conhost and Windows Terminal both support VT once ENABLE_VIRTUAL_TERMINAL_PROCESSING is set on stdout. member.name: T:winapp2ool.WebViewScaffolds
member.summary:
Shared, use-case-agnostic substrate for embedded-Chromium FileKey emission. Consumed by entry generators (UWPBuilder, EntryBuilder) that need a curated, consistent set of cleaning targets for an application's embedded WebView2 / EBWebView or QtWebEngine data folder.
The module is engine-family-neutral: a single section-prefix parameter selects which family of scaffold sections to read from a catalog, so multiple catalogs can be processed by the same loader. The shipping families are:
WebViewScaffold — WebView2 / EBWebView layout ( Assembler\Scaffolds\webview.ini ), templates use the %WebViewRoot% placeholder.
QtWebEngineScaffold — QtWebEngine layout ( Assembler\Scaffolds\qtwebengine.ini ), templates use the %QtWebEngineRoot% placeholder. QtWebEngine bundles an older Chromium with a flatter on-disk layout (no Default\Network\ subfolder, no privacy-sandbox surface), so it warrants a separate catalog rather than reusing the WebView2 paths.
Source files contribute [{Family}: Name] sections whose FileKeyBase= values use a family-specific root placeholder. Callers parse their own source files, delegate scaffold sections to (or load a whole catalog via ), resolve the active selection via , and later substitute their own host-specific root paths into the resulting templates.
The placeholder is implementation-neutral by name: a UWP consumer feeds it the %LocalAppData%\Packages\...\EBWebView form, while a win32 consumer would feed the host-relative data folder under %LocalAppData% , %ProgramData% , or wherever the host stores its data. The library is agnostic to root-path conventions; callers handle their own variable expansion before passing the resolved root to the emitter.

member.name: F:winapp2ool.WebViewScaffolds.DefaultScaffolds
member.summary: Default scaffold names emitted when a caller requests WebView2 scaffolding without an explicit selection list. Limited to low-risk categories that are safe for any WebView-hosting application; host-risk categories (cookies, history, session, web storage) require explicit opt-in by the caller.

member.name: F:winapp2ool.WebViewScaffolds.QtWebEngineDefaultScaffolds
member.summary: Default scaffold names emitted when a caller requests QtWebEngine scaffolding without an explicit selection list. Broader than : QtWebEngine's catalog splits two low-risk targets into their own scaffolds that the WebView2 catalog leaves bundled behind host-risk gates — StorageQuota (a rebuildable quota accounting file) and VisitedLinks (a link-coloring bloom filter, which QtWebEngine-hosting application shells have no UI for). Both are default-on here because the hand-written entries this catalog replaces treated them as routine cleaning. Host-risk categories (cookies, history, session, site storage) still require explicit opt-in.

member.name: M:winapp2ool.WebViewScaffolds.ParseSection(winapp2ool.iniSection2,System.Collections.Generic.Dictionary{System.String,System.Collections.Generic.List{System.String}},winapp2ool.MenuSection,System.String)
member.summary: Parses a [{prefix} ...] scaffold section, collecting its FileKeyBase= values into keyed by the scaffold's name (the portion of the section header after , trimmed). Warns on unrecognised key types and on duplicate scaffold names (last definition wins).

member.name: T:winapp2ool.ExpansionDomain
member.summary: The domain a key value lives in, used to decide how undeclared <token> references are resolved. Filesystem keys (FileKey, DetectFile, etc.) cannot contain literal < or > because those are reserved Win32 path characters; registry keys can. The engine therefore drops filesystem keys that carry an undeclared token (hard error) and lets registry keys keep the literal bracket (advisory only).

member.name: F:winapp2ool.ExpansionDomain.Registry
member.summary: The key value will be written into a registry location (RegKey, RegKeyBase, Detect, ExcludeKey with Reg flag). Undeclared <token> references pass through verbatim with an advisory diagnostic.

member.name: M:winapp2ool.VariableSet.Add(System.String,System.String)
member.summary:
Adds a variable declaration with values parsed from a comma-separated list. Trimmed, non-empty tokens only. Re-adding an existing name replaces the prior values.
Splitting is bracket-aware: only commas at <> depth zero separate values, so an inline list inside a declaration — e.g. Root=HKCU\...\<6.0,7.0,11.0>\... — survives as a single value for the expander to fan out later, instead of being shredded into broken fragments at the inline list's commas.
member.param: The variable name (case-insensitive)

member.name: M:winapp2ool.VariableSet.SplitTopLevelCsv(System.String)
member.summary: Splits a declaration value on its top-level commas — those at <> bracket depth zero — leaving commas inside an inline <a,b,c> list intact. <> nesting is forbidden by the token grammar, so a simple depth counter suffices; an unbalanced < keeps the remainder on one value, which is harmless for the malformed input that would produce it.
member.param: The raw declaration value to split
member.returns: The value split on top-level commas only; inline-list commas are preserved

member.name: T:winapp2ool.VariableExpander
member.summary:
Shared cross-DSL preprocessing engine that fans one template out over a set of declared list variables. Variables are declared as entry-level keys (e.g. Version=9.0,10.0,11.0 ) and referenced via <name> placeholders inside other key values; the engine returns one expanded string per cartesian combination of the variables present in the template, with leftmost-first occurrence varying slowest (outermost loop). A placeholder body containing a comma ( <a,b,c> ) is an inline ad-hoc list — an anonymous axis declared at its use site, for one-off leaf lists not worth a named declaration.
The engine is string-generic — it knows nothing about winapp2 key types, ini parsing, or output formatting. The caller passes one template at a time, tags the call with an (so the engine can apply the filesystem-vs-registry rule for undeclared tokens), and routes any returned values onto its own logging surface.
This module is the phase-2 pass in the two-phase builder DSL pipeline. Phase 1 is each builder's own %% environment-style substitution (e.g. %WebViewRoot% , %Package% ), which runs first and produces the templates fed to this engine. The two phases compose because their token domains are closed: %% expansion never emits <> tokens and this engine never emits %% tokens.

member.name: F:winapp2ool.VariableExpander.TokenPattern
member.summary: Regex matching one <name> placeholder. The body ( [^<>]+ ) requires at least one character and forbids nesting, so a stray < or > elsewhere in the template is left alone. Compiled once at module load.

member.name: M:winapp2ool.VariableExpander.Expand(System.String,winapp2ool.VariableSet,winapp2ool.ExpansionDomain,System.String)
member.summary:
Expands a template into its fan-out over the declared list variables it references. Returns one string per cartesian combination, with leftmost-first occurrence varying slowest. A template with no declared tokens returns a single-element list containing the template verbatim.
A token whose body contains a comma is an inline ad-hoc list — e.g. <System32,SysWOW64> is an anonymous two-value axis, fanned out exactly like a declared variable but without a separate declaration. It is the natural form for a single-use leaf list. Two different inline lists in one template cross-product like any two axes; an identical inline list repeated in one template co-varies (one axis) and emits an Advisory, because an anonymous list cannot state same-axis intent — declare a named variable when co-variance across positions is wanted. Inline detection takes priority over the declared-name lookup, but declared names never contain commas in practice so the two never collide.
Undeclared <name> tokens are resolved by : filesystem keys drop the template (empty plus a Warning diagnostic), registry keys keep the literal text and emit an Advisory. A referenced variable with an empty value list also drops the template with a Warning.
The engine itself produces no logging — every diagnostic is returned in for the caller to route onto gLog / MenuSection.AddWarning . is embedded verbatim in diagnostic messages so the caller does not need to wrap them in another format string.
member.param: The single key value to expand. May contain zero or more <name> tokens at any position, including inline <a,b,c> ad-hoc lists

The entry's declared variable set. Tokens whose name is declared in are expanded; others are handled per . Each declared token observed is marked referenced on for the caller's later typo backstop check.
Whether is a filesystem-domain or registry-domain key value. Determines the behavior on undeclared tokens
Caller-supplied label (e.g. entry name and key type) embedded into any returned diagnostic messages
member.returns: The expanded value set and any diagnostics raised during expansion

member.name: M:winapp2ool.VariableExpander.ResolveAll(winapp2ool.VariableSet)
member.summary:
Resolves nested <name> references inside the value lists of itself, before any user template is expanded. Each variable's values are fanned out against the variables they reference, in topological order so each dependency resolves before its dependents. Cyclic dependencies are detected and left unresolved with a Warning.
After this call returns, every variable's value list contains literal strings (or, for variables in a cycle, the original templated strings). User templates that reference these variables therefore receive fully-resolved substitution without the engine needing a second expansion pass.
Reference tracking on IS updated during resolution: a variable consumed only via a nested chain (e.g. RegRoots=...<HKLMVersions>... with no template referencing <HKLMVersions> directly) still counts as referenced, so the unreferenced-variable typo backstop does not false-positive on it. A variable declared but reached by neither a user template nor a nested chain remains unreferenced and is reported by .
member.param: The variable set to resolve in place
member.returns: Diagnostics raised during resolution — cycle warnings, undeclared-token advisories inside variable definitions, etc. The caller routes them onto gLog / MenuSection.AddWarning .

member.name: M:winapp2ool.VariableExpander.SubstituteTokens(System.String,System.Collections.Generic.Dictionary{System.String,System.String})
member.summary: Replaces every <name> token in that matches an entry in with the corresponding value, case-insensitively. Tokens not present in are left literal so registry-domain undeclared tokens survive untouched.
member.param: The string in which to substitute tokens
The current iteration's variable-name → value bindings (case-insensitive)
member.returns: The template with all matching tokens replaced

This runs before the command line (and therefore SuppressOutput ) is parsed, so we also pre-scan the raw args for -s mirroring the -offline pre-scan in to avoid briefly resizing a window that silent mode is about to abandon. member.name: T:winapp2ool.FlavorizerSettings
member.summary:
Holds the settings for the Flavorizer module, which provides a user interface for applying "flavors" (sets of modifications) to ini files.
The flavorization process uses multiple correction files applied in this order:
Section Removal ( File3 ) — Remove entire sections
Key Name Removal ( File4 ) — Remove keys by name matching
Key Value Removal ( File5 ) — Remove keys by value and keytype matching
Section Replacement ( File6 ) — Replace entire sections
Key Replacement ( File7 ) — Replace individual key values
Section and Key Additions ( File8 ) — Add new sections and keys
All correction files are optional. The flavorization process skips any that are not specified or do not exist.

member.name: T:winapp2ool.Flavorizer
member.summary:
The Flavorizer module provides a user interface for applying "flavors" to ini files. A flavor is a set of modifications that adapt a base ini file for specific use cases.
The flavorization process applies modifications in this specific order:
Section Removal — Remove entire sections
Key Name Removal — Remove keys by name matching
Key Value Removal — Remove keys by value and keytype matching
Section Replacement — Replace entire sections
Key Replacement — Replace individual key values
Section and Key Additions — Add new sections and keys
If a modification file is not present, that modification step will be skipped.
This module wraps Transmute.Flavorize with an intuitive UI for managing the multiple correction files used in the flavorization process, and also provides the ability to auto-detect a group of flavor files within a target directory.

member.name: T:winapp2ool.Transmute
member.summary:
Transmute (formerly Merge ) is a winapp2ool module which provides the ability to modify an iniFile2 object using the contents of a separate iniFile2 object with conflict resolution at different levels of granularity.
In the parlance of Transmute, there are two files of interest:
The 'base' file and the 'source' file
The 'base' file is the one whose content will be modified by the operation. That is, this file will be either added to, removed from, or have some or all of its content modified
Likewise, the 'source' file is the one from which the modifications will be provided. That is, this file will have its content added to, removed from, or replace content in the 'base' file
Transmute modes:
Add (Default transmute mode)
Adds sections to the base file from the source file
If a section from the source file exists in the base file, the individual keys will be added
Replace
Replace has two sub modes: BySection and ByKey
ByKey (Default replace mode): Replaces the value of keys in the base file with values from the source file based on their Name
BySection: Replaces entire sections in the base file with the section of the same name in the source file.
Note: Replace does nothing with sections from the source file not found in the base file
Remove
Remove has two sub modes: BySection and ByKey
ByKey (Default remove mode): Removes keys from individual sections within the base file
Keys must be provided within a section in the source file and will be removed from the corresponding section of the same name in the base file
Remove Key Modes:
ByName : Removes keys based on matching key names only
Removing a key with this mode requires knowledge of its Name. This works best for unnumbered keys (in the context of winapp2.ini, keys like Section, or unnumbered Detection keys) but also works for numbered keys if you know the number. For numbered keys it is generally best to try using the ByValue remove mode
ByValue : Removes keys based on matching key values. The KeyType (key name without numbers) must also match. Works best for numbered keys whose numbers may change or be unclear when invoking Transmute
Additionally, Transmute provides an important function called Flavorize. Flavorize is used to apply "flavors" to an ini file. In the context on winapp2.ini, there has historically existed at least one flavor: the "non-ccleaner" file. Flavorize automates and also democratizes what has historically been a very labor intensive process: Maintaining a concise set of transformations on the base winapp2.ini that can be used to adapt it to different purposes. The flavorization process always takes in a base ini file and then applies operations in the following order:
Section Removal -> Key Name Removal -> Key Value Removal -> Section Replacement -> Key Replacement -> Section and Key Additions
member.remarks:
Remarks:
Transmute replaces the Merge module and has has three modes which are wholly discrete from one another. This is a breaking change from old versions of Merge prior to 2025, which always add entries which don't exist and perform conflict resolution as part of that process.
As the functionality of Merge evolved, it no longer felt appropriate to refer to its output as the result of a "merger" necessarily. We now consider the resulting output a Transmutation. Nevertheless, this is still spiritually the Merge module

member.summary:
Steps through the sections in the and applies the transmutation to each. Sections found in the not found in the when the transmutator is not Add will be ignored with an error message
When RecognizeGlobalSections is enabled, three sentinel section names are processed before any named sections, so that specific per-section operations can refine the result of global ones:
[*Map: label] sections define key mapping rules (Replace ByKey mode only)
A [*] section applies its keys to every section of the base file
[*Name: scaffold] sections apply their payload keys to every base section whose name ends with " scaffold *" and which satisfies the section's Match= predicates (engine in tool/TransmuteNameFilter.vb )

member.name: M:winapp2ool.Transmute.applyGlobalSection(winapp2ool.iniFile2@,winapp2ool.iniSection2,winapp2ool.MenuSection@)
member.summary:
Applies the keys of a [*] sentinel section to every section in the under the current transmute mode.
Section-level modes are refused with a warning: Remove BySection would empty the file and Replace BySection is incoherent as a global operation. Numbered keys are refused in Add mode because adding them to every section creates instant duplicates.
Key values containing the %EntryName% token (case-insensitive) have the token replaced with each receiving section's name as the key is applied, enabling per-section values from a single global key (eg. ID=%EntryName% ). The token is only recognized here — named-section operations leave it literal.
Unlike named-section operations, a global operation expects most sections not to match, so per-section misses are silent: the menu receives one summary line per source key and per-hit detail is written to the log

member.name: T:winapp2ool.TransmuteNameFilter
member.summary:
Implements Transmute's [*Name: scaffold] sentinel: a name-filtered global operation. Where [*] applies its keys to every section, a [*Name:] section applies its payload keys only to base sections selected by two orthogonal filters — an anchored name suffix and an optional set of content predicates.
The section header carries a scaffold label; a base section is selected when:
1. its name ends with " scaffold *" (case-insensitive, anchored on the winapp2 entry terminator so "… Web Browsing Session *" does not also catch "… Web Browsing Session Backups *" ), AND
2. it satisfies the rule's Match= predicates — no predicates means the name filter alone decides; otherwise the section must contain at least one key matching any one predicate (KeyType equal, value equal or glob-matched; OR-semantics across the set)
The two filters do different jobs: the name suffix selects which scaffold, the predicate set confirms what kind of entry (eg. that it is a browser via Match=Section=* Web Browser ). The predicate set cannot separate one scaffold from another, so the anchored suffix must carry that distinction.
Every key that is not a Match= key is payload, applied under the current transmute mode. Payload values support the %EntryName% token like [*] . In Add mode a payload key already present in a selected section is skipped, so the operation never duplicates an existing key

member.name: T:winapp2ool.TransmuteKeyMap
member.summary:
Implements Transmute's [*Map: label] key mapping rules: source-file sections which match keys anywhere in the base file by KeyType and Value, and replace the whole key — including its Name — with one or more replacement key lines. This is the only Transmute operation able to change a key's Name, which makes data-driven category conversions possible (eg. Section=Google Chrome Web Browser → LangSecRef=3029 )
Rule sections contain:
Match=<Name>=<Value> — repeatable (as Match1= , Match2= , ...). A base key matches when its KeyType (Name with numbers stripped) and Value both equal the match key's, case-insensitively — consistent with Remove ByValue matching. A match Value of exactly * matches any value of that KeyType; because rules are first-match-wins, a wildcard rule placed last serves as a fallback behind more specific rules
Replace=<Name>=<Value> — repeatable (as Replace1= , Replace2= , ...). The full replacement key line(s). The first replacement takes the matched key's ordinal position and any remaining replacements are inserted immediately after it in file order, so a single rule can de-abstract one key into several (eg. a wildcard DetectFile into hardcoded per-variant paths). Replacement key numbering is the rule author's responsibility — keys are written as given, consistent with Add mode
Rules are applied in a single pass in file order with first-match-wins semantics: each base key is evaluated against its original value only, so a key replaced by an earlier rule is never re-matched by a later rule in the same run, and inserted replacement keys are never evaluated at all. Replacement happens in place, preserving the section's key order

member.name: T:winapp2ool.BrowserBuilder
member.summary:
BrowserBuilder is a winapp2ool module which handles the generation of bespoke winapp2.ini entries for a very large number of web browsers. It provides a small scripting interface which allows for the dynamic creation of entire groups of winapp2.ini entries using a limited set of easily accessed information.
All input files are read from a single configurable source directory. At minimum, that directory must contain at least one of chromium.ini or gecko.ini - the specially formatted ruleset files that drive entry generation. BrowserBuilder is primarily intended as a small devops tool but end users might find it useful as it enables them to generate entries for non-standard installation paths or portable applications while keeping winapp2.ini up to date separately
Additionally, and because it is intended to simplify the devops, Browser Builder expects to "Flavorize" the browsers.ini that it produces. This is done so as to resolve over and under coverages by generated entries as well as resolve incompatibilities. Accordingly, it expects but does not require a set of Flavor correction files in the source directory (up to 1 "Add" file, up to 3 "Remove" files, and up to 2 "Replace" files) - all resolved by canonical name. Consult the Transmute documentation for more information about Flavors
Unflavored browser.ini files may be broken or incomplete depending on use case

member.name: T:winapp2ool.Trim
member.summary:
Trim is a winapp2ool module that evaluates the detection criteria of each entry in a winapp2.ini file against the current machine and removes any entries whose detection criteria are not satisfied, producing a system-specific subset of the full database.
The full winapp2.ini database contains entries for thousands of applications, the vast majority of which will not be installed on any given machine. Trimming eliminates those irrelevant entries, reducing load time for cleaning software (particularly CCleaner) and avoiding spurious scans.
Detection criteria and evaluation order:
DetectOS
Evaluated first. If present and not satisfied by the current Windows version, the entry is immediately discarded without checking any other criteria.
If satisfied and no other detection keys are present, the entry is retained.
DetectOS values take the form VERSION| (minimum), |VERSION (maximum), or VERSION1|VERSION2 (range), where version numbers are major.minor doubles (e.g. 6.1 for Windows 7, 10.0 for Windows 10).
Detect
Registry paths checked for existence. If any Detect key matches a registry key present on the current system, the entry is retained.
DetectFile
Filesystem paths (supporting wildcards) checked for existence. If any DetectFile key matches a file or directory present on the current system, the entry is retained.
SpecialDetect
Deprecated CCleaner variable checked against a hardcoded list of well-known browser/application install locations. Supported values: DET_CHROME , DET_MOZILLA , DET_THUNDERBIRD , DET_OPERA . If the corresponding application is detected, the entry is retained. Parsing for this is left only to support very old versions of winapp2.ini.
Entries with no detection keys of any kind are always retained.
Include and exclude overrides:
When enabled, the includes file ( TrimFile2 ) and excludes file ( TrimFile4 ) each contain a list of entry names (one per ini section header) that unconditionally override the normal detection evaluation. An entry whose name appears in the includes file is always retained regardless of whether its detection criteria are satisfied. An entry whose name appears in the excludes file is always removed regardless of whether its detection criteria are satisfied. Include and exclude checks run before any detection evaluation.
Environment variable expansion:
In addition to standard Windows environment variables, Trim resolves several CCleaner-specific variables that do not exist natively in the Windows environment:
%Documents% %UserProfile%\My Documents on XP; %UserProfile%\Documents on Vista+
%CommonAppData% %AllUsersProfile%\Application Data on XP; %AllUsersProfile%\ on Vista+
%LocalLowAppData% %UserProfile%\AppData\LocalLow
%Pictures% %UserProfile%\My Documents\My Pictures on XP; %UserProfile%\Pictures on Vista+
%Music% %UserProfile%\My Documents\My Music on XP; %UserProfile%\Music on Vista+
%Video% %UserProfile%\My Documents\My Videos on XP; %UserProfile%\Videos on Vista+
%ProgramFiles% receives special handling: paths under %ProgramFiles% are checked against both the native-bitness Program Files directory and the 32-bit Program Files (x86) directory on 64-bit systems, so entries covering 32-bit applications installed on 64-bit Windows are retained correctly.
VirtualStore augmentation:
For entries that pass detection, Trim inspects the entry's FileKeys, RegKeys, and ExcludeKeys and generates additional keys covering VirtualStore locations that correspond to paths found under %ProgramFiles% , %CommonAppData% , %CommonProgramFiles% , and HKLM\Software . VirtualStore keys are only appended when the corresponding VirtualStore path actually exists on the current system, ensuring the output remains accurate to the machine.

member.name: T:winapp2ool.LintReconciler
member.summary:
Guards the generative modules' normalization pass with a semantic reconciliation: the optimization pass is only permitted to make formatting-level changes (key reordering and renumbering, FileKey pattern-list alphabetization, and merging FileKeys that share a path and flag). Any change that loses or rewrites cleaning content — a dropped entry, a discarded malformed key, a rewritten value — indicates the generator emitted invalid data, which the linter then silently destroyed. That is a correctness bug in the generator or its sources, not a cleanup, so the gate reports every such difference, dumps the pre-optimization file next to the output for forensics, and fails the build (nonzero exit code) in scripted use.
The comparison decomposes each entry into a set of semantic units: each FileKey contributes one path|pattern|flag triple per semicolon-delimited pattern (via ), and every other key contributes its number-stripped KeyType=Value pair. Units are compared case-insensitively as sets, which makes the three sanctioned optimization classes invisible by construction: reordering and renumbering do not change set membership, pattern sorting does not change the triple set, and a merge of two same-path FileKeys produces exactly the union of their triples. Everything else — in either direction — is reported. Detection is default-deny: a future lint rule that changes semantics will fire this gate until its behavior is explicitly accounted for.
Reporting (but never detection) pairs a lost unit with a gained unit into a single old → new rewrite finding when the pairing is unambiguous: FileKey triples that agree on two of their three components, or any other key type with exactly one lost and one gained unit. Anything that cannot be paired one-for-one stays reported as separate lost/gained findings.

member.name: M:winapp2ool.LintReconciler.remotedebugGuarded(winapp2ool.iniFile2,System.String,winapp2ool.MenuSection)
member.summary: Runs with full optimizations over and reconciles the result against the input. When the pass made only formatting-level changes, behaves exactly like remotedebug(givenIni, True) . When semantic differences are found, writes the pre-optimization content to <name>.prelint.ini alongside the output, reports every difference, and sets a nonzero process exit code so scripted builds fail.
member.param: The generated iniFile2 to normalize; its Dir and Name determine where the forensic pre-lint dump is written on gate failure
The generative module's name, embedded in gate messages for source-of-warning localisation
The MenuSection receiving gate warnings for display
member.returns: The normalized iniFile2 , exactly as returns it (the gate reports but does not roll back)

member.name: M:winapp2ool.LintReconciler.PairRewrites(System.Collections.Generic.List{System.String},System.Collections.Generic.List{System.String})
member.summary: Pairs lost units with gained units where the correspondence is unambiguous, removing paired units from and in place. FileKey triples pair when exactly one lost and one gained triple agree on two of their three components — the disagreeing third is the rewrite — with the most specific passes running first so a flag change is not misread as a pattern change. Every other unit pairs when its KeyType carries exactly one lost and one gained instance. Ambiguous groups (more than one candidate on either side) are left untouched.

member.returns: Pairs of (old unit, new unit) for each rewrite found; empty if none qualify
